notes:
PatchStream Labs builds a developer IDE and CI-native copilot used by their engineering teams and selected enterprise customers. Primary interest: tool/function calling for code agents — run unit tests, lint, collect build logs, and return structured results into the IDE. Requirements summary: 
- Low tail latency for completions and streaming start (aiming for <100ms start, <50ms per-token for inline completions).
- Function calling that can securely execute test runners (pytest, jest) inside ephemeral sandboxes with strict resource limits and network isolation.
- Model/version pinning so SDK teams can freeze a model for the copilot while Redwood optimizes behind the scenes.
- Deterministic outputs for snapshots; need a way to tag model + quantization profile per workspace.
- Routing/fallback: prefer a high-quality 70B variant for enterprise workspaces, fallback to a smaller quantized 13B when capacity or cost limits hit.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency per invocation, plus per-route traces connected to CI job ids.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, KMS keys for secrets used by sandboxes, audit logs retained for 1 year, and data residency controls for EU customers.

POC notes and results so far: 
- Internal demo of function-calling succeeded: agent invoked a sandboxed container, ran unit tests, returned structured JSON (tests/passed/failed) and uploaded zipped logs to their internal storage.
- Perf: average test-run orchestration overhead ~1.6s for small suites; need optimization for micro-feedback (<1s).
- Cost-sensitivity: engineering org self-funded; looking for predictable per-seat/month plus burstable capacity pricing.

Quotes and character notes: 
- CTO (R. Chen): "We will not ship any executor that can reach prod networks until legal signs off. Auditability is non-negotiable."
- Head of Platform: wants a canary rollout for model pinning and automatic fallback policy integrated into Redwood Console.

Open items: 
- Legal to approve agent execution privileges (deadline: 2025-03-01).
- Finalize SOW and pricing (expecting Redwood dedicated or private).
- Confirm support for their custom test-runner hooking into function-calling API (they will provide spec).

Suggested Redwood approach: propose Private deployment (VPC) POC with minimal on-prem connectivity, include SE-led security deep dive, provide an Optimize runbook for batching/caching and quantization profiles for their common repos.
